ideas.title: Lightning makes magnets
ideas.critique: Lightning-made lodestones are a real and rarely seen phenomenon, and a field solved from the bolt's path plus a remanence per spike by angle and distance is new physics that puts em.jl's current field to work; the morning compass round gives the storm a result to read. The weak points are the bolt's path chosen by a 'tallest iron wins' rule, which is a script rather than a discharge, and a loop that waits for weather the player cannot call, so planting is a guess more often than a skill.

ideas.title: Read the sand, find the stone
ideas.critique: This is round 1's iron sand again, now with a real goal: reading depth and pose from the pattern and then digging to check turns the textbook picture into a puzzle that changes every game. Thousands of interacting dipoles on the GPU that chain by themselves are the strong part; if the patterns are not clearly different for depth and orientation, the reading turns into guessing and the film is just the filings picture everyone knows.

ideas.title: An iron tree on the stone
ideas.critique: It is the iron beard from round 1 with a stacking record added, and the picture (spikes clinging to the stone) is what the last post showed, only bigger. Solving every spike together and letting joints fail by force is the actual road step after s148's two-spikes-hold result, and a tower that collapses spike by spike gives the player a skill and a reason to try again.

ideas.title: Stroke a needle into a compass
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
same_form: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: A compass from a needle is the exact example the big goal names, and a close film of a tool working a material and showing its new state is the form of the wire and glass posts. A real hysteresis curve per segment feeding the floating bowl is honest and useful later as a measuring instrument, but someone watching sees a needle stroked and then swing, which is what everyone already expects to happen.
